Track bar up = looser (more lateral weight transfer to outside rear, less side bite). Track bar down = tighter. Each inch of bar height change has a predictable effect on handling balance.
Tractive Force = (HP × 550) / Speed (fps). Shows how much force is available vs traction limit — tells you if you're wheel-spin limited.
If your loan payoff exceeds your car's trade-in value, you're "upside down" — that difference gets rolled into your next loan, increasing what you owe on the new vehicle.

Drag = ½ × Air Density × Drag Coefficient × Frontal Area × Speed². A large, boxy trailer typically has both a much higher drag coefficient and far more frontal area than the tow vehicle alone, which is exactly why aerodynamic drag climbs so much while towing at highway speed.

Axle Load = Trailer Weight − Tongue Weight. Whatever weight isn’t riding on the tow vehicle’s hitch is carried by the trailer’s own axle(s) — the figure to check against the trailer’s axle and tire capacity ratings.

Cargo Capacity = Trailer GVWR − Empty Trailer Weight. How much the trailer itself can be loaded with cargo, water, and gear before hitting its own weight rating — separate from (and in addition to) the tow vehicle’s own payload limit.

Estimates sway risk from tongue weight %, trailer length, weight-distribution hitch use, and trailer-to-tow-vehicle weight ratio. Low tongue weight and long trailers without WD hitches are the biggest sway contributors.
Compares actual axle load to total tire capacity. Trailer tires (ST-rated) have less margin than passenger tires — running at or above rated capacity is a leading cause of trailer tire blowouts.
Gearhead Labs Premium unlocks Transmission Cooler Sizing — size an ATF cooler from your actual heat-rejection target instead of a generic cooler-by-horsepower chart.

entries.definition: The ratio of input-shaft to output-shaft speed of the transmission in a given gear.

entries.description: Cross-checks a claimed dyno/estimated HP number against actual trap speed performance. Useful for verifying tune claims, comparing combos, or catching gearing/aero issues.

Weight = (π÷4) × (Outer Diameter² − Inner Diameter²) × Length × Material Density. The actual weight of a piece of round tube stock — useful for chassis, roll cage, or driveshaft weight estimates before cutting material.
Gearhead Labs Premium unlocks Tuned-Pipe Length — the effective expansion-chamber length for a tuning speed from exhaust duration and gas temperature.

Compressor Power = Mass Flow × Specific Work. The actual mechanical power a turbo’s turbine (or a supercharger’s belt drive) has to supply to compress a given air mass flow to its target pressure ratio.

Use the free Turbocharger Airflow calculator to establish your baseline airflow numbers. Premium’s Turbo Sizing turns that into a compressor selection workflow. (For the complete compressor map, see E01 in the Engineering Lab.)

Boosted Airflow = Naturally-Aspirated Airflow × Boost Multiplier. The actual airflow a turbocharged or supercharged engine flows once boost is added — the number that then drives injector, MAF, and turbo sizing.
Turning Radius = Wheelbase / sin(Steer Angle). Shorter wheelbase and more lock = tighter turning circle.

entries.definition: The angle between the two shafts joined by a universal joint. A single U-joint running at an angle makes the output speed fluctuate twice per revolution; equal and opposite angles at the two ends of a driveshaft cancel it.

entries.description: For smooth operation, front and rear U-joint angles should be within 1° of each other and under 3° each.
Simple strategy model: pit-lane time loss divided by lap-time advantage. Traffic, tire warm-up, safety cars and track position are outside this model.

Kus = Wf/Cf − Wr/Cr, in deg/g. Wf = W × front %/100 and Wr = W × (100 − front %)/100 are the front and rear AXLE loads (lb); Cf and Cr are the front and rear AXLE cornering stiffnesses (lb/deg). Positive = understeer, negative = oversteer, zero = neutral. Cornering stiffness comes from tire data or estimated from tire construction and pressure.

Convert common automotive units with explicit SI factors. Liquid Volume (gallons, quarts, cups, fl oz) is kept separate from geometric Volume (cubic inches, cubic feet) — pick whichever matches what you’re actually measuring.
Every 1 lb of unsprung weight (wheels, rotors, axles) has roughly 5× the negative effect of sprung weight on handling. Reducing unsprung weight is one of the highest-value suspension upgrades.

Gearhead Labs Premium unlocks Valve Acceleration — the inertial loading your valvetrain and springs must control through the lift event.
Curtain area = π × valve diameter × valve lift.

Flow Coefficient = CFM ÷ (Valve Area × √Pressure Drop). A comparative flow index for a port or valve at a given flow-bench test pressure — useful for comparing two ports tested at the same pressure, not as an absolute 0-1 discharge coefficient.
Gross valve lift = cam lobe lift × rocker ratio. Net lift is gross lift minus the specified lash. Pushrod length is not part of this simple lift calculation.

Valve Lift = Cam Lobe Lift × Rocker Ratio. The gross valve lift a given cam lobe and rocker arm combination produces, before subtracting any mechanical-lifter lash (see the Valve Lash calculator for net lift).

Valve Lift = Cam Lobe Lift × Rocker Ratio. The gross valve lift a given cam lobe and rocker arm combination produces, before subtracting any mechanical-lifter lash (see the Valve Lash calculator for net lift).
Gearhead Labs Premium unlocks Valve Motion Velocity — how fast the valve is actually moving at any point in the lift event, not just how far it opens.

Open Force = Seat Load + (Spring Rate × Lift). The valve spring force at a specific valve lift, given the spring’s installed seat load and rate — the number that has to be checked against the valvetrain’s actual load capacity at maximum lift.
Basic helical compression-spring rate: k = Gd⁴/(8D³Nₐ). D is mean coil diameter and Nₐ is active coils. Open pressure is seat pressure plus spring rate × valve lift.
Effective ratio is measured valve lift divided by measured cam/lobe lift.
Shows gross lift, entered lash and a simplified net-lift estimate. Actual dynamic behavior can differ with rocker geometry, deflection and hydraulic-lifter behavior.
Calculates optimal velocity stack (air horn) length for peak power at target RPM. Longer stacks = lower RPM peak. Shorter = higher RPM.
Maximum rate of climb in feet per minute. VCR = (HP × 33,000 × eff) / weight
Voltage Drop = Current × Wire Resistance. The real voltage lost along a wire run before it reaches the load — the direct check for whether a wire gauge is adequate for a given current and run length.
Convert between gallons, quarts, pints, liters, and more.
VE = Actual Airflow / Theoretical Max × 100. Peaks at peak-torque RPM. Stock street 75-85%, modified NA 85-95%, NA race 95-105%.
Gearhead Labs Premium unlocks Von Mises Stress — distortion-energy equivalent stress with a Tresca comparison and safety factors.

Wastegate Flow = Total Exhaust Flow × Desired Bypass Fraction. How much exhaust flow actually needs to bypass the turbine through the wastegate to hold a target boost level, rather than driving the turbine further.
Calculates a target injection flow from a user-selected lb/hr-per-HP ratio. The ratio is an engineering starting assumption, not a universal requirement.
A Watt's link constrains lateral axle motion. A Panhard bar follows an arc; for a horizontal bar, the lateral shift at vertical travel h is L − √(L²−h²).

inputs: Vertical Suspension Travel from Ride Height

entries.description: "Wedge" = cross weight percentage above 50%. "Bite" = right rear minus left rear weight. Adding a round of bite (tightening LR jacking bolt) loads the LR, loosening the car. Every 1 turn ≈ 20–30 lbs.
Circle track targets: Left side 53–57%, Rear 51–55%, Cross 49–51% for neutral oval handling. Dirt cars run more left weight.
Every pound saved is worth HP at the track. Uses the formula: HP Gain = HP × (weight reduction / new weight).

Longitudinal weight transfer under braking or acceleration — enter a positive G-force either way. For a version that also tells you which axle gains the load, see Braking Weight Transfer or Acceleration Weight Transfer.

entries.definition: The change in vertical tyre load between front and rear (under acceleration or braking) or between left and right (in a corner), caused by the centre of gravity being above the ground.
entries.distinctions: It is load moving between tyres; the vehicle's total weight does not change.

entries.description: Gearhead Labs Premium unlocks Weld Fillet Strength — throat, allowable stress and load of a fillet weld on the AWS / AISC basis.
Gearhead Labs Premium unlocks Weld Heat Input — arc energy and process heat input from voltage, current and travel speed.
Wet bulb temperature accounts for evaporative cooling. Used for jetting and precise DA calculations.
Wheel Rate = Spring Rate × Motion Ratio². Motion ratio = wheel travel / spring travel.
Offset (mm) = (Backspace − (Rim Width/2 + 0.5)) × 25.4. Positive offset pushes wheel inward; negative pushes out.

entries.definition: The effective spring rate measured at the wheel: the spring rate multiplied by the square of the motion ratio (spring travel over wheel travel).

related.note: Wheel rate = spring rate × motion ratio².

entries.description: Ramp Travel Index (RTI) style score: (ramp height climbed ÷ wheelbase) × 1000, both measured in the same units. This mirrors the widely used off-road ramp-travel-index convention. It is a comparative score, not a certified competition result — an official score requires a standardized ramp and a static measurement procedure.

Recommended minimum line pull = GVWR × recovery difficulty multiplier (1.5x is a common baseline; 2x or higher for mud, steep incline or single-tire recovery). Mechanical advantage with N snatch blocks in a simple doubled-line rig is modeled as 2^N — a stated rigging assumption, not a universal constant, and real-world friction loss will reduce it somewhat.
Headwind hurts; tailwind helps. Approx 0.001 sec per mph of headwind, 0.001 sec gain per mph of tailwind.
Gearhead Labs Premium unlocks Wing Aspect Ratio — span, chord and planform area, plus the induced-drag coefficient that aspect ratio drives.
Gearhead Labs Premium unlocks Wing Center of Pressure — where a wing’s resultant force acts along the chord, from the section’s CL and moment coefficient.
Downforce uses D = ½ρV²ClA. This version uses positive Cl as downforce magnitude and a separate Cd for drag, avoiding the previous sign ambiguity and the incorrect Cl×0.3 drag shortcut.

Wing Force = ½ × Air Density × Force Coefficient × Wing Area × Speed². The same aero force equation applied specifically to a single wing element, whose own force coefficient is usually higher than a whole vehicle’s, since a dedicated wing is a much more efficient aero device per unit area.

Required Current = Electrical Load ÷ System Voltage. The current a wire and its fuse actually need to carry for a given accessory’s power draw — the number that determines minimum wire gauge and fuse rating.
Calculates minimum wire gauge from amperage, run length, and allowable voltage drop. Always use the next larger gauge when in doubt.

Yaw Moment = Tire Force × Lever Arm. The rotational (yaw) effect a tire’s lateral force produces around the vehicle’s center of gravity — the fundamental building block behind how a car actually rotates into and out of a turn.
